chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

In every two hundred dirhams of silver, there are five dirhams; and if it falls short, there is no zakat upon you. And from gold, for every twenty dinars, there is half a dinar; and if it falls short, there is nothing upon you.

key_terms.دِرْهَم: Dirham, a silver coin used as a unit of currency and weight for zakat calculation
key_terms.دِينَار: Dinar, a gold coin used as a unit of currency and weight for zakat calculation
key_terms.زَكَاة: Zakat, the obligatory alms-tax or purification payment
key_terms.نِسَاب: Nisab, the minimum threshold of wealth above which zakat becomes obligatory

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of silver and gold required to pay zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the classical nisab thresholds for silver (200 dirhams) and gold (20 dinars), reflecting the monetary standards of the early Islamic period. It clarifies that partial amounts below these thresholds do not incur zakat, a principle widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence for determining the minimum wealth liable for purification. The narration underscores the precision required in calculating zakat on precious metals, linking material wealth to spiritual obligation.
